opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams and marketing. Up 22% YoY — growing, but slower than revenue.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI products. Up 15% YoY; includes $256M of stock-based pay.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Roughly flat, up 1% YoY.

follow100Note: Snowflake spent $117.01 of every $100 it took in on direct and running costs — more than it earned — and other income covered only $4.83 of the gap, leaving a $12.39 loss per $100. The spending rows add to $100.01 due to rounding.
footerNote: Snowflake reports in thousands (revenue was $1,546,793K); figures here are rounded to $M, and other income is shown as $74M (exact $74.7M) so the rounded $M lines foot exactly. Excluding stock-based pay and other non-GAAP items, operating income was $237M (a 15.3% margin). Chart note: Snowflake's running costs exceeded its gross profit by $263M and other income covered $74M of that, so the chart draws the remaining $192M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source, which also covers the $3M tax bill.
otherDetail: Other income of $74M, net: $42M of interest income and $35M of other income, less $2M of interest expense (exact total $74.7M before $M rounding).

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Customers pay to store data and run computing and AI workloads on Snowflake's platform, billed by how much they use. Up 37% YoY and 96% of all revenue.

segments.name: Professional services and other
segments.note: Help getting set up and moving data onto Snowflake, plus other small items. Roughly flat, up 1% YoY, and it costs more to deliver than it brings in.

takeaways.text: Product revenue rose 37% to $1.49B — the third straight quarter of faster growth — and Snowflake raised full-year product revenue guidance to $6.07B, up 36%.
takeaways.title: Product growth is speeding up

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $263M. The main reason: $456M of stock-based compensation (paying staff in shares) counted as a cost this quarter. Leaving that and similar items out, non-GAAP operating income was $237M.
takeaways.title: Still a GAAP loss, mostly stock pay

takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — revenue customers have contracted but not yet used — hit $9.0B, up 30%, and 828 customers each spent over $1M in the past year, up 27%. Free cash flow was $84M.
takeaways.title: Customers keep committing more

verdict: Snowflake's revenue grew 35% to $1.55B as product revenue accelerated for a third straight quarter — but $456M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $263M and a net loss of $192M.
